questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was far away, and a culture that i otherwise never engage with. I also didn't want a place were english was too common.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A memory for life.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Korea is different of course. But generally you can find guides in english. If you do a bit of research before leaving, it will not be too scary.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Korea University has a "buddy system" which means that local korean students are assigned to different groups. You could always text your buddy if you had any questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They know what they are doing, you are not the first exchange student to go there. The orientation was, however, extremely long and full of information, and it was 36 degrees celcius that day... They are very thorough in Korea.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is difficult unless you are okay with living in a "Gosiwon" also called "Staytel" or "Gositel". It is infamously pretty bad 1-room "apartments", and they are all over Seoul. Otherwise finding living accommodoations can be a bit difficult because of the language barrier. I stayed in a Gosiwon for 4 months and it was bad, but since i was never home anyway, it didn't matter.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The Gosiwons can definitely work, if you have a small budget. But if you want a proper apartment, go on facebook and find groups that are about rental spaces in Seoul. Maybe have a back-up hostel plan in mind. If you have a friend to go with, you can split the rent and live quite nice and cheap.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Gosiwons are always available. So you are never gonna be homeless.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: So much unnecessary information. They will send you so many documents, with very very detailed information.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They required proof that you had a certain amount of money, or that your parents had. And then of course you had to go to the embassy to apply for your study visa. Then the University sends you a LOT of information. You have to read it thoroughly. Luckily they also outline the application process in steps, so you know what to expect.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could e-mail the university, but they prefer that you just read the application material thoroughly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. But you have to stay up until 3am in the morning to register, because it is on a first-come-first-serve basis. Some people even go to high-speed internet cafés just to have a higher chance of getting competitive classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read the materials, and take notes, so you don't feel stressed.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses provided in english are for exchange students mostly. For humanities, the courses are very easy. Plan your schedule, so your classes end early, or so you have few days with classes.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: If you just study a little bit, you'll be fine. I took Korean Language I, and that was hard. Everything else was extremely easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Many multiple choice quizzes and basically no readings. Mid-term exams and final exams are equally important. You cannot miss classes, because that will affect your grade. Otherwise the style of teaching is very methodical and thorough, but in a way that makes it easy to grade you on wether or not you were listening to the professor. Just show up, take basic notes and you'll get an A.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Korean Language I
Popular Culture
Composers of Classical music
The Genre of Classical Music
Ancient Chinese Law and Philosophy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Ancient Chinese Law and Philosophy was super interesting. Learning Korean is also amazing, and very rewarding.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *

Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *

Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: NHIS - National Health Insurance. They require you to sign up to an insurance that costs about 375dkk per month.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is not expensive, but you'll often eat out as the way to be social. Housing was cheap if you choose Gosiwon, and transportation was only 300dkk per month, and i used it every single day.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are clubs, but they are hard to join as an exchange student. However it is possible if you make sure to look into it.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The buddy system was great! We often went out for drinks and food with all the other exchange students and the other Korean Buddies. A lot of music festivals and other excursions are also available.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: So much. Go hiking. Go to Sokcho. Go to Busan. Go on a Temple stay. There is an infinite amount of delicious food. Go clubbing in the safest environment i've ever been in. Go visit Jeju Island. There are so many things to do.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Grab drinks with koreans, and go on hikes and trips to Busan and Jeju.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Koreans can be shy, but generally very welcoming and polite. If you are respectful and kind, you will make a lot of friends.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the KUBA events. The buddy system will help you meet many different people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Seoul is a busy city, and you can feel that. They are more conservative in many ways when it comes to the body, yet I never felt that personally, but it is noticeable. Some few places they didn't really want foreigners, but it was very rare.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the Korean culture in general. Very polite and nice all around, and i never felt unsafe anywhere i went. Just be respectful and you'll be welcomed.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't be a "Koreaboo". Just because you like K-Pop and K-Dramas, it does not mean you know what it means to be Korean. They have a tough history, and you should be respectful of the fact that it is not like you see on TV. 

Go and listen to undergound music! There are so many artists and cool venues. Be curious! 

Try to get some Korean friendships! It is so valuable and awesome to not feel like a tourist. Actually hanging out with locals that can give you advice and perspectives is amazing.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You will have to get something called an Alien Registration Card! If you want the best experience, get it yourself, and not through the institution. It will go much faster, and you need it for many things.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships i made. For sure. The moment it felt like i actually lived in another country, was also pretty cool. Learning Korean was a part of that.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I went on a very slim budget. I had to really be careful about spending too much money. If you are smart and save up, you'll be fine.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Korea University was a great experience. I can't recommend it enough. But don't go because you think the classes will be amazing. Go and engage yourself in the history and culture. Learn the korean writing language "Hangul" before you go. It is actually much easier than you think, and it will help you a lot.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
